question: If {2^x} = {3^y} = {6z}, then (1)/(x) + (1)/(y) - (1)/(z) is equal to :
solution:
__Concept:__

ax × ay = ax+y.

 a⁻x = (1)/(a^x).

 a^x=k Rightarrow a = ktfrac{¹{x}}.

__Calculation:__

Let 2x = 3y = 6z = k.

∴ 2 = ktfrac{¹{x}} ...(1)

 3 = ktfrac{¹{y}} ...(2)

 6 = ktfrac{¹{z}} ...(3)

∵ 2 × 3 = 6

∴ ktfrac{¹{x}}times ktfrac{¹{y}}=ktfrac{¹{z}} ...[Using equations (1), (2) and (3)]

⇒ ktfrac{¹{x}+tfrac{1}{y}}=ktfrac{¹{z}}

⇒ (1)/(x)+(1)/(y)=(1)/(z)

⇒ (1)/(x)+(1)/(y)-(1)/(z)=0.
